cards.heading: The mask splits the address
cards.body: A prefix like /26 means the first 26 bits identify the network and the remaining 6 bits identify hosts. 2^6 = 64 addresses per subnet, 62 usable.
cards.example:
/26 = 26 network bits + 6 host bits
2^6 = 64 addresses, 64 - 2 = 62 usable

cards.heading: Block size
cards.body: Find the 'interesting' octet (where the mask is neither 255 nor 0). Block size = 256 - mask value in that octet. /26 -> mask 255.255.255.192 -> block size 64.

cards.heading: Find the network
cards.body: Round the interesting octet DOWN to a multiple of the block size. 192.168.1.130/26 -> 130 rounds down to 128 -> network 192.168.1.128.

cards.heading: Broadcast and range
cards.body: Broadcast = next network - 1 (192.168.1.191). Usable hosts are everything between: .129 to .190.
cards.example:
next network = .192, so broadcast = .191
hosts .129 - .190 (62 usable)

cards.heading: When the interesting octet isn't the last
cards.body: The same method works in any octet. Find the octet where the mask isn't 255 or 0, take its block size, round down there, and set every octet after it to 0 for the network or 255 for the broadcast. The first usable host is the network + 1; the last is the broadcast - 1. Usable hosts = 2^(host bits) - 2.
cards.example:
172.16.45.200/20: mask 255.255.240.0, block 16 in octet 3
45 rounds down to 32 -> network 172.16.32.0
next network 172.16.48.0 -> broadcast 172.16.47.255
12 host bits -> 2^12 - 2 = 4094 hosts

cards.heading: Sizing subnets
cards.body: For a number of hosts, find the fewest host bits h where 2^h - 2 is big enough; the prefix is 32 - h. For a number of subnets, borrow the fewest bits n where 2^n is big enough and add n to the starting prefix. A /22 holds 2^(26-22) = 16 /26 subnets: each extra prefix bit doubles the count.

cards.heading: VLSM and overlapping subnets
cards.body: VLSM (variable-length subnet masking) uses different prefix lengths in one network. Allocate the largest subnet first, then put each next subnet at the next free address. Two subnets overlap if one's range (network to broadcast) contains any part of the other's; a shorter prefix that starts at or before a range and ends at or after it contains it.
